review: The game looks exciting, has huge potential. I love the community so far, giving it a try for sure!

One day in the year 2000 I stumbled across a simple looking game called Uniball and decided to give it a try.
Years later, I finally started going to meetings to break the habit.

Now Uniball has been revamped and made available on Steam; and I'm enjoying every minute of my relapse!


Uniball is a game that can be enjoyed differently at all levels.
You'll learn how to play within a minute, but it'll take thousands of hours to come even close to mastering this highly competitive e-sport!
Simple concept and can be challenging at first, but a lot of fun and very addictive.
"Es la polla"

If I had to describe this game in one word... Addicting, (in a good way of course). But seeing as this is a review let's mention everything. 

The Pros are as followed.  Fast and frantic fun at it's best, with crisp controlls that never hinders the enjoyment of the game, a great community, (though small but that's for cons) diffenent maps which is unique to a sports game and great game mechanics which are easy to learn and hard to master.

There are not is but two cons that will only really be fixed by time. Those are the small player base, (which based on the fun quick gamplay should be fixed soon) and the amount of pro to new player ratio, (seeing as this game is over 15 years old) which should be fixed with more new players, (hopefully).

Now that pros and cons are out the way a couple things that may be either bad or good, (prefrence). For a game 15+ years old it does have flash like graphics, (a crunchball 3000 feel {if you don't know that game I'm sorry}) It's controlls take some time to get use to (but hey I mean so does Rocket League) and lastly the little dot circle around your ship to show where the ball is isn't needed on smaller levels, (Not acually bad if you learn <<F3>> Disables it, so yeah remember F3).

All in all this is one of the most refreshing games I've played in a long time and it's FREE and you can't beat free, So why not try it and see for yourself I'm nearly Positive you won't regret it.

Uniball is an older "classic" style game we were accustomed to playing growing up. It's the type of game that is easy to jump into and play, but requires time/practice if you want to hang with the best competitively. I played it a handful of times 10+ years ago. I come from another "oldie but goodie" game (ARC) that has no direct connection, but is fairly familiar to each other. It's refreshing to see that Uniball has withstood the years, despite some hardships perhaps, and is now on steam thriving. Since joining the lobby and playing a bit the last couple days, the current community already in place has been nothing but courteous and willing to help in any way they can. Very newbie friendly, which is a rarity in online gaming these days. I'm a bit jealous, as I see mostly the opposite on ARC on a regular basis. I would highly recommend giving UniBall a shot if you are looking for something that can offer that nostalgia some of us older gamers enjoy while still being challenged from a competitive standpoint.

Uniball is one of the few games that I've played that is entirely skill based.  The basic mechanics are simple and the ships perform identically, which allows individual skill and team play to dictate the outcome of games.  Good players and teams will seldom lose to opponents with less skill, but really this is how it should be and is no different than any other sport played on a field or court.

But this shouldn't discourage newer players.  The game is a blast to play at any level of skill and the staff and player base are eager to help new players find their way.

In addition, it's possible to create private games where new players can play against their equally newbish friends and be terrible together, which is actually a lot of fun.

UniBall is one of the longest-standing games on the internet.

It has been in beta, for several years, and seen many periods of isolation from its players, though, presently, a lot of the old players are coming back. It expresses a great learning curve, though it may seem built for the elites, this game teaches things about movement, intuition, teamplaying, and how to work with another person on the internet.

In fact, I believe if you become skilled at playing UB, your intuition, and natural abilities IRL will improve since it is such a profoundly unique game to natural physics; employing "gravity" and ship movements based perhaps on actual laws of this world.

If you were to play UniBall tonight, you would likely see a large number of faces to whom were once players of this game well over ten, to even fifteen years ago, however, you will also find a great degree of respect toward the new player, since this is by far one of the most challenging games to learn in a day.

I myself have played UB for over 16 years, which began in late 1999.

In spite of UniBall's learning curve, however, I have noticed a great and rather profound degree of skill in the new player recently. The fact that it took me (myself) over three months to master dribbling, I have somewhat found myself very impressed with some of the skill in the new players of UB.

Tutorials, articles, and etc. will be written to advance the first few days of the new player, if not by myself, then by other players, and hopefully all of the vets, and new players, alike, can get along in this terribly unique game.

Please log in with hope, and don't disregard the fact that this is a very different game from most games on the internet. It is, in my opinion, the "best" game on the internet. I have held true to this opinion for the entirety of my career there, and I have even played with its original creator, to whom I once interviewed, a very skilled programmer. The resident programmers of UB have great skill, and also the administration of UB has proven very effective over the past few years.

One last mention is a man named "Zoop" who you may see in the chatroom. If you see him, don't be afraid to ask for help. He will give you guidance, because he truly cares about the game of UniBall. 

This game is worth playing. It deserves attention. And it needs new players.

-Brendan

Luckily there are always "noob" games available to jump into, and the community is very open to new players.  There is something incredibly satisyfing about going head to head with opponents and beating them with creative plays and teamwork.
